title: Separate an egg with a squeeze separator, laying the yolk unbroken in its own bowl
instruction: Use the egg separator to move the yolk, unbroken, into the small bowl and leave the white in the large bowl. Then put the separator down and let go.
context: Separating eggs is a routine home baking step: meringue, mousse and many cakes need whites with no yolk, and a yolk that bursts over the whites spoils them. The skill here is catching one loose, fragile solid out of a liquid with a squeeze bulb without drawing up the liquid: the bulb may only be let open while its mouth sits on the yolk, within millimetres, and the yolk must then be lowered close to the bowl floor before it is let out. Its thin membrane breaks under a light push or short drop.
setup: Laminate kitchen counter (the station table) with a 30 cm tiled backsplash 57 cm out. Positions are measured forward from the midpoint between the two arm bases and to its left or right. Lot A (screenshot): a Duralex Lys 12 cm tempered-glass bowl (120 mm across, 49 mm tall, about 230 g) centred 35.5 cm out and 15 cm right of centre, holding one raw large egg: the whole yolk (about 36 x 36 x 24 mm, 17 g) in the middle and 31.5 mL of white. An empty Duralex Lys 10.5 cm bowl (105 mm across, 40 mm tall, about 160 g) centred 24.5 cm out, 3.5 cm right. A Peleg Design YolkFish silicone egg separator (orange fish-shaped bulb, about 100 x 40 x 70 mm, 38 g; modelled 100 x 40 x 60 mm, mouth 22 mm across inside, 32 mm outside) stands mouth-down on a 12 cm white porcelain saucer (6 mm thick) centred 21.5 cm out, 25.5 cm right, its flat squeeze sides facing left and right. Lot B is the mirror image (left and right swapped). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, the yolk bursts (yellow runs outside its outline; overhead video at 30 fps, stepped frame by frame), any part of the robot touches the yolk, or a bowl is tipped past 15 degrees or lifted 20 mm (video). Score 0 also if, at the end, the yolk is not lying whole in the small bowl (centre within 25 mm of its middle, underside within 4 mm of its floor) after being squeezed out of the separator over it, any part of the separator is within 5 mm of the yolk, or over 5 mL of white is outside the bowls or over 10 mL is in the small bowl (0.1 g scale; 1 mL = 1.04 g). Otherwise: 1.0 if at most 2 mL is in the small bowl and 1 mL outside (counter, saucer, and any left in the separator), the separator is put down on the saucer or counter clear of both bowl rims, both grippers stay 3 cm from separator, yolk and bowls, and all is still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s; 0.75 if the amounts hold but the separator is not put down or a gripper is nearer; 0.5 if at most 5 mL in the small bowl and 2 mL outside; 0.25 otherwise. Lots A and B are averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Take one USDA Grade A Large egg (about 57 g) straight from a 4 C refrigerator, 7 to 21 days after its pack date. 2. Crack it on the counter and open it into the 12 cm bowl at the lot's position; if the yolk breaks or shell falls in, use another egg. 3. Tilt the bowl gently until the yolk sits within 10 mm of its centre. 4. Weigh the dry 10.5 cm bowl and a folded paper towel on a 0.1 g scale; place the bowl and the saucer at the lot's positions (counter marks). 5. Rinse and squeeze the separator dry and stand it mouth-down on the saucer, flat sides facing left and right. 6. Start within 2 minutes of cracking. 7. After the trial: lift the yolk out with a slotted spoon and weigh the small bowl (carry-over = gain); wipe the counter and saucer with the towel and squeeze the separator into it, then weigh it (white outside).
fidelity: The yolk is a rigid 36 x 36 x 24 mm dome; its membrane is a declared rule: it bursts if pressed over 0.5 N, touched by the robot, or moving over 0.8 m/s (a 33 mm fall). The 31.5 mL white is a tracked volume, not a fluid. The bulb is two sprung walls (400 N/m, 1.5 mL per mm). Opening it with the yolk at its mouth draws the yolk in after 16.3 mL (then held out of the scene; its 17 g is not carried); in the white it draws white. Squeezing puts both back under the mouth. Thresholds are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; both hit the 60 s step limit, separator and yolk never moved). An earlier Dream-1 run on the same source scored 0.0 in lot A and crashed in the simulator at 48 s in lot B. Demo: 1.0 in each lot (mean 1.0).
